threads.thread_goal: Align on current pain points and approve target tax workflow scope.

messages.text: Good morning all, kicking off the Standardised Tax Documentation and Filing Workflow Rollout for project_title: Standardised Tax Documentation & Filing Workflow Rollout. The aim is to map our current process, agree on a target workflow, and then maintain a clear workflow map and RACI. I will start with T1 to map current processes and T4 for roles and responsibilities, which will feed into A1. Before I schedule interviews, we need to align on which departments and processes are in scope for this first phase. My initial proposal: accounting, finance, and operations, focusing on quarterly and monthly tax filings plus supporting documentation. Please share any missing areas or concerns so we can lock the scope.

Thanks for starting this. From a tax side, I agree accounting, finance, and operations should be in the first wave. I would also include any data flows from sales that impact VAT and from HR if there are payroll-related taxes, even if we only map them at a high level in A1 for now. For processes, I suggest we cover: periodic VAT filings, corporate tax prepayments, withholding tax, and any statutory books updates that feed tax numbers. That should give us enough coverage without blocking on every edge case.

Agree with the departments listed so far. From my experience in bookkeeping, operations sometimes sends cost data late, which affects VAT and corporate tax. For T1, I can help interview accounting and finance to capture where delays usually happen and how they hand over documents. Maybe we mark in A1 where we have recurring late inputs so we can address them later with reminders.

I can support with mapping how sales and legal share documents today, especially contracts and special terms that may affect tax treatment. For T1, I will need a bit of guidance on how detailed the process map in A1 should be. Are we aiming for every single step, or just main steps, owners, and tools used

For A1, I suggest we keep it at the level of main steps, owners, and tools, plus key handovers. We can add notes for known bottlenecks rather than mapping every micro-step. That should be enough for T1 and will make T4 easier when we draft the RACI. If everyone agrees, I will prepare a simple template for the interviews so we capture the same information from each department.

I can help with scheduling and note-taking for the interviews under T1, especially with operations and sales. One question on scope: do we include incident handling for tax discrepancies now, or is that part of a later task like T12

For now, I would only map where discrepancies typically surface in the current process, for example during reconciliations or before filing. The detailed incident handling procedure is indeed T12 and will come later. But it is useful if A1 already shows where issues are detected and who is involved, so we can design a cleaner path when we get to that step.

On departments in scope, I support including accounting, finance, operations, sales, and HR, at least where they feed tax-relevant data. That will make T4 more complete when we define responsibilities. Maybe we can treat HR and sales as lighter touch in A1, focusing on their data outputs and deadlines rather than their internal steps.

Works for me. I will focus my T1 notes on main steps and handovers. For processes, can we confirm that the initial scope is: VAT filings, corporate tax prepayments, withholding tax, and statutory books updates that impact tax numbers If yes, I will use those as headings when I talk to sales and legal so they know what to prepare.

Yes, those four process groups cover the main recurring filings. We can add smaller items later if needed, but for the first version of A1 and T4, that list is enough. I will validate the draft map once you have it, to make sure the tax steps and deadlines are correctly reflected.

Summarising scope so far: departments included are accounting, finance, operations, sales, and HR where they provide tax-relevant data. Processes included are VAT filings, corporate tax prepayments, withholding tax, and statutory books updates that feed tax figures. Unless there are objections today, I will treat this as our agreed initial scope for T1 and T4 and reflect it in A1.

No objections from my side. For ownership of A1 and the RACI in A5 later, I suggest one of us in the management assistant group takes it, with tax reviewing. Given you started T1 and T4, would you be comfortable being the main contact for maintaining the workflow map and RACI, while I support with updates

I agree that it is better to have a single main contact for A1 and A5. I can help with version control and filing in the shared drive, but I think it is clearer if one person coordinates content changes and approvals with the tax team.

From tax side, I am fine with 109659 being the main contact for A1 and A5, as long as we keep a simple change log so we can show internal audit how the workflow and RACI evolved. I will review any updates that touch tax legislation or filing responsibilities before they are finalised.
Works for me as well. I will support with collecting updates from operations and sales when their steps change, and pass them to 109659 so A1 and A5 stay aligned.

Happy to take on ownership for maintaining the workflow map A1 and the RACI matrix A5. I will coordinate content changes, keep a simple version log, and route anything tax-sensitive to 66260 for review. Unless anyone disagrees, we can record that as the decision on ownership.
All good from my side. Once you have the first draft of A1 from T1, please share it here and I will add comments on tax steps and any missing controls before we move on to the detailed RACI under T4.

Great, I will schedule the interviews for T1 with accounting, finance, operations, sales, and HR, and then share the first version of A1 here for review. After that we can start drafting T4 and A5 based on the agreed scope and handovers.

threads.thread_goal: Design and sign off templates, tracker, and checklist for tax documentation.

messages.text: Following the process mapping, I have prepared first drafts for the tax documentation templates under T2 and a basic structure for the tracker in T3. The templates cover invoice summaries, deductions, and adjustments, and I have checked them against current tax rules. For the tracker A2, I set up columns for document type, period, owner, due date, status, and comments. I would like your feedback on both the templates and the tracker structure before we move towards a pre-filing checklist A4.

Thanks for sharing. Looking at the invoice summary template from T2, I like that you separated taxable and non-taxable amounts. One suggestion: could we add a field for the source system or file name This helps when we reconcile with accounting records. For A2, I wonder if we should also have a column for department, so we can filter by accounting, operations, sales, etc.

I reviewed the deductions template. It looks clear, but I am not sure if non-finance staff will understand all the tax terms. For T2, could we add short explanations or examples for fields like adjustment reason and tax base change Maybe we can later reuse those explanations in the checklist A4 so people know what to double-check before filing.

On A2, I like the basic structure. I am just not sure how we will track escalations for late documents. Is that part of T3 or will it be handled later under T9 Maybe we should at least have a status like pending reminder or escalated so we can see where we stand.

From an operations and scheduling view, A2 will be our main tool to keep everyone aligned. I support adding department and maybe a simple priority flag for items that are critical for the next filing. For T3, we also need to make sure quarterly and annual deadlines are clearly visible, maybe with a separate tab or a filterable view.

Good points. I can add source system or file reference to the invoice summary template and a department column to A2. For the tracker under T3, I will also add a simple priority field so we can highlight items that block filings. I will keep the structure lean so it stays easy to maintain in a spreadsheet.

On the deductions template, I agree that some terms may be too technical. I will add short descriptions and one example line for each section as part of T2. Later, when we build the checklist A4, we can reference those examples so staff know what to look for. That should also help when we prepare the broader guidelines.

Regarding escalations, the detailed rules will be defined in T9, but I agree A2 should at least show the status. I will add status values like pending, reminder sent, escalated, and completed. That way, when we implement T9, we can link the reminder schedule to these statuses without changing the tracker structure.

For the pre-filing checklist A4, I suggest we mirror the main sections of the templates from T2: invoices, deductions, adjustments, and statutory books. Each line could say something like invoice summary for period X reconciled with accounting and signed off by Y. That will make it easier for teams to confirm they used the right template and filled all mandatory fields.

Agree on having a clear view of deadlines in A2. Maybe we can freeze the header row and use conditional formatting to highlight items due within 3 days. I can help set that up in the spreadsheet for T3, as long as we keep the number of columns manageable.

That would be helpful. Once the structure of A2 is agreed, I can support with a short how-to section so departments know how to filter by department, period, and status. This will also be useful later when we run the pilot and need to track which documents are still missing.

I like the idea of aligning A4 with the templates. I will draft A4 with sections for invoices, deductions, adjustments, and statutory books, each with a short description and a sign-off field. This will sit on top of the templates from T2 and the tracker A2, so teams can quickly confirm everything is ready before filing.

Before we finalise, can we confirm which fields in A2 are mandatory I assume period, document type, owner, due date, and status must always be filled. It would be good to agree now so we can explain it clearly during training.

Yes, I propose the following mandatory fields in A2: period, document type, department, owner, due date, and status. Priority and comments can be optional. For the templates under T2, all tax-relevant numeric fields and the sign-off fields should be mandatory. If everyone agrees, I will lock those columns in the spreadsheet and mark mandatory fields clearly in the templates.

Mandatory fields list works for me. On the templates from T2, I have no further comments after your updates. They cover the data we need for VAT and corporate tax and are still readable. I think we are ready to treat these as our standard templates, subject to any minor tweaks after the pilot.

I am aligned as well. The templates are structured and the tracker fields are clear. From a non-finance perspective, the added explanations and examples should help a lot. I do not see any blockers to using these as the standard going forward.

Same here. The templates under T2 and the tracker structure in A2 and T3 look ready to use. I suggest we formally confirm that these are our standard templates and tracker structure for the rollout, and we will only adjust them after the pilot if needed.

Thanks all. To close this out: we will adopt the current versions of the invoice summary, deductions, and adjustments templates from T2 as our standard tax documentation templates, and we will use the agreed A2 tracker structure with the mandatory fields we listed. Any further changes will be based on pilot feedback. I will mark these versions as baseline for the rollout.

threads.thread_goal: Lock roles, responsibilities, and reminder/escalation rules.

messages.text: I have drafted the RACI matrix for the new tax workflow under T4 and a first version of the reminder and escalation plan from T9. Both are summarised in A5. The RACI covers VAT, corporate tax prepayments, withholding tax, and statutory books updates, with roles for accounting, finance, operations, sales, HR, and tax. The reminder plan proposes weekly reminders for upcoming deadlines and a two-step escalation for missing data. I would like your review so we can agree on the final roles and reminder rules.

Thanks for pulling this together. In A5, I see tax marked as accountable for final filings and consulted on most data preparation steps, which matches how we work. One adjustment: for statutory books updates that directly impact tax numbers, tax should probably be accountable together with accounting, not just consulted. On T9, weekly reminders might be too frequent for some items; maybe we can tie the frequency to how close we are to the filing date.

Looking at A5, I like that operations and sales are clearly responsible for providing data, not just informed. For VAT, I would mark accounting as responsible for reconciling invoice summaries with the ledger, with tax accountable for the final return. That will help avoid confusion when something is missing. On T9, I agree with 66260 that we should increase reminder frequency as we get closer to the deadline.

From a coordination side, A5 looks mostly clear, but I am not sure HR will understand their role in withholding tax just from the matrix. Maybe we can add a short description in the guidelines later. For T9, I suggest we define a standard pattern: for example, first reminder 10 days before due date, second reminder 5 days before, and escalation 2 days before if data is still missing.

On T9, do we already know who the escalation contacts are for each department For example, for operations would it be the operations manager or the team lead I want to make sure we do not escalate to the wrong person and create confusion.

Good point. In the draft T9 plan, I proposed the department manager as the second-level escalation contact, with the regular data owner as the first contact. For operations, that would be the operations manager; for sales, the sales manager; for HR, the HR manager. I will add these names explicitly in the reminder schedule so it is clear who gets notified when.

I like the pattern you suggested. For T9, we can standardise it as: first reminder 10 days before due date, second reminder 5 days before, and escalation 2 days before if status in A2 is still not completed. For very small items we can skip the first reminder, but the general rule will help everyone know what to expect.

Agree with that schedule. We should also make sure the reminder text clearly states which items in A2 are pending and what the impact is if they are late. That will make the reminders more actionable and reduce back and forth.

On A5, I support marking tax as accountable together with accounting for statutory books updates that affect tax. I can help adjust the matrix so that for those steps, accounting is responsible and tax is accountable, with finance consulted. That should also align with how internal audit sees the control structure.

I will update A5 accordingly: for statutory books updates that feed tax numbers, accounting responsible, tax accountable, finance consulted. For VAT, accounting responsible for reconciliations, tax accountable for the return. For withholding tax, HR responsible for data, tax accountable for filings. I will also add a note that HR will get a short explanation in the guidelines so their role is clear.

With those adjustments, the RACI in A5 reflects how we actually work and what tax rules require. From my side, the matrix is ready to be treated as final for this rollout, and we can reference it in the guidelines and training.

The reminder schedule sounds clear now. Just to confirm: first reminder 10 days before, second 5 days before, escalation 2 days before, using the status in A2 to decide who to contact. If that is correct, I can help draft the reminder and escalation email texts under T9.

Yes, that is the pattern we will use. I will document it in the T9 plan and link it to the statuses in A2. For escalation contacts, we will use department managers as second level, as discussed. Once the texts are drafted, we can reuse them for both email and messaging reminders.

From my side, both the RACI in A5 and the reminder plan in T9 are clear now. I do not have further changes. Once we confirm, I can help share a short summary with accounting and operations so they know what to expect before the next filing cycle.

To close this thread: we are confirming the updated RACI matrix in A5 as the agreed view of roles and responsibilities for the new tax workflow, and we are adopting the reminder and escalation rules under T9 with the 10-5-2 day pattern and department managers as escalation contacts. These will be our reference for the rollout and the pilot.

threads.thread_goal: Plan and debrief the pilot run of the new workflow.

messages.text: I would like to propose our first pilot for the new tax workflow under T7. My suggestion is to use the next monthly VAT filing for the domestic entity as the pilot period. Scope would include: using the new templates from T2, tracking all documents in A2, applying the pre-filing checklist A4, and logging any discrepancies in A7. We will then review the results and update the guidelines A3 and incident procedure T12 as needed. Please share if this scope and period work for you.

Using the next monthly VAT filing as the pilot makes sense to me. It is frequent enough that we can quickly apply lessons learned. For T7, I suggest we limit the pilot to domestic transactions only, at least for this first run, so we do not mix in complex cross-border cases. We can still log any issues in A7 and see how the templates and A2 behave.

From a coordination side, the proposed period works. We just need to make sure operations and sales are aware that their data for that VAT period must go through the new templates from T2 and be tracked in A2. For A3, it might help if we prepare a short one-page summary of the pilot rules so they know what is different from the usual process.

I agree with focusing on the next monthly VAT filing. One question: during the pilot, if we find that some teams struggle with the templates, do we log that in A7 as an incident or just as feedback for T8 I want to be sure we do not overuse the incident log.

Good question. For the pilot under T7, I suggest we use A7 only for issues that could affect tax correctness or filing timeliness, such as missing documents, wrong amounts, or late approvals. Usability feedback on templates can go into a separate feedback list for T8. That way, A7 stays focused on discrepancies and we still capture improvement ideas.

I support using the next monthly VAT filing as the pilot and limiting it to domestic transactions as 27135 suggested. For T7, I can coordinate with operations and sales so they know which period is in scope and that they must use the new templates and A2. We should also schedule a short review meeting right after the filing to go through A7 and the checklist A4.

For the pre-filing checklist A4 during the pilot, I can run through it together with accounting before we submit the VAT return. That will help us see if any checklist items are unclear or missing. I will note any issues so we can feed them into T8 and the guidelines A3.

For the review meeting after the pilot, we should invite at least one person from each involved department plus tax. We can structure the discussion around A7 incidents, checklist A4 findings, and general feedback on A2 and the templates. I can help capture actions and owners so they feed directly into T8.

So to summarise the pilot proposal: period is the next monthly VAT filing for the domestic entity, scope limited to domestic transactions, using templates from T2, tracker A2, checklist A4, and incident log A7. If there are no objections, I would like to confirm this as the agreed pilot scope for T7.

No objections from me. I will help keep A2 updated during the pilot and make sure any incidents that meet the criteria you described are logged in A7. I will also collect usability feedback separately for T8.

All good from my side. I will coordinate with accounting on the checklist A4 and make sure we follow the new workflow end to end during the pilot. Any gaps we find will go into the list for T8 and also help refine the incident procedure under T12.

I will draft a short pilot summary based on A3, explaining to departments what is in scope, which period we are testing, and what they need to do differently. That should reduce confusion and help us get cleaner feedback.

After we run the pilot and hold the review meeting, I will consolidate all feedback and incidents into T8. That will include template changes, checklist A4 adjustments, and any updates needed for the guidelines A3 and the incident procedure T12. We should aim to complete those updates before the following VAT filing so we can benefit immediately.

When you consolidate T8, please flag any changes that affect non-finance teams so we can highlight them in the next training and communications. I will also check that A2 and A4 reflect the final agreed changes so there is a single source of truth.

Once T8 is done, I propose we lock the updated templates, checklist A4, guidelines A3, and incident procedure T12 as the standard set for the broader rollout. Any further changes would then go through a simple change request so we keep A7 and A8 consistent for audit purposes.

I agree. Based on what we already see in the current drafts, I expect we will mainly adjust wording and add a few extra checks, not redesign everything. Once we have the final set after T8, we can also start preparing input for the post-rollout report A8.

To close this: we are confirming the next monthly domestic VAT filing as the pilot period and scope for T7, and we agree that after the pilot we will adjust templates, checklist A4, guidelines A3, and the incident procedure T12 under T8 based on the feedback and incidents logged. Those updated versions will become our standard set for the wider rollout.

threads.thread_goal: Coordinate training sessions and final rollout communication.

messages.text: With the pilot plan in place, I have prepared draft training slides A6 and a tentative rollout timeline under T6. The training covers the new workflow, templates, tracker A2, checklist A4, and key points from the guidelines A3. The timeline proposes training sessions next week and go-live for the full workflow in time for the next quarterly tax filing. I would like your input on training dates, attendee groups, and whether the proposed go-live date is realistic.

I reviewed A6. The flow is clear, especially the part where you show how A2, the templates, and A4 connect. For attendee groups, I suggest we have at least three sessions: one for accounting and finance, one for operations and sales, and one for HR and other support teams. That way we can tailor examples to each group. For timing, next week works for me as long as we avoid month-end closing days.

On A6, I would add a short section on where to find the guidelines A3 and the RACI A5, so people know where to look after the training. For T6, I agree with three sessions. We should mark attendance as mandatory for data owners in each department, and optional but recommended for their backups.

For scheduling under T6, I can help coordinate with operations and sales to find slots that do not clash with their peak times. Maybe late morning works best for them. Also, we should plan to share the slides A6 and a short summary afterwards for those who cannot attend live.

From tax side, the proposed go-live before the next quarterly filing is feasible, provided we complete the pilot adjustments in time. In A6, I will add a brief section on common tax errors and how the new workflow and A4 help prevent them. For attendee groups, I agree that data owners should be mandatory participants.

For the go-live date, we should also consider time to update statutory books alignment under T11 and to start collecting baseline data for the post-rollout report T10. If we go live right after the pilot adjustments, we will still have enough time before the quarterly deadline to stabilise the process.

Agree. For T11, I can help review the statutory books checklist and make sure it reflects the new workflow and responsibilities from A5. We should do that before the first full quarter under the new process so we do not miss any required records.

I will update A6 to include links to A3 and A5 and clearly mark which parts of the training are mandatory for data owners. For dates, how about we schedule: accounting and finance on Tuesday morning, operations and sales on Wednesday late morning, and HR and support on Thursday afternoon next week I will check with department managers to avoid critical closing days.

Those days work for me. I will start drafting the invitations for T6, listing the mandatory attendee groups and linking to A6 and A3. I will also mention that the new workflow will become the default for the next quarterly filing, so people understand the timing.

I confirm availability for accounting and finance on Tuesday morning. I will encourage team leads to bring real examples so we can walk through A2 and A4 live during the session. That usually helps people understand how the tracker and checklist work in practice.

I will join the operations and sales session on Wednesday and help explain how their data flows into A2 and the tax filings. I can also take notes on any questions that might require updates to A3 or the templates after T8.

On the go-live date, I propose we set the full workflow go-live for the start of the next quarter, right after we complete T8 and update A3, A4, and A6. That gives us one monthly pilot plus time to adjust, and still meets the requirement to be live before the next quarterly filing. Does that timing work for everyone

Start of next quarter works for me. It gives us time to adjust statutory books under T11 and to start capturing data for T10. We can use the first quarter under the new workflow as the comparison period for the post-rollout report A8.

I am aligned with that go-live date. It will also make it easier to communicate to departments: from the first day of next quarter, all tax-relevant documents must follow the new workflow, templates, and A2 tracker.

Works for me as well. I will make sure the training invitations and follow-up notes clearly state that the new process becomes mandatory from the start of next quarter and that we will monitor on-time submissions and error rates for T10.

To summarise training: we will run three sessions next week, grouped by department as discussed, with attendance mandatory for data owners and recommended for backups. Slides A6 will be updated with links to A3 and A5, and we will share materials and a short summary afterwards. I will treat these dates as confirmed unless someone raises a conflict today.

And to close on timing: we are confirming the start of next quarter as the go-live date for the full tax workflow, after we complete T8 and update A3, A4, and A6. From that date, all departments will use the new templates, tracker A2, and checklist A4, and we will start collecting data for the post-rollout report T10 and the statutory books alignment T11.
